title: Federica Torgneur (Founder & CEO, Reveevo · ex-McKinsey · INSEAD MBA) — 'Someone had put into writing everything I had been thinking about building mission-driven businesses'
summary: Federica Torgneur — founder & CEO of Reveevo (mission-driven circular resale platform for home goods; ex-McKinsey; INSEAD MBA) — publishes a rich recap after completing the Incorruptible Early Stage Founders Cohort, the six-week program led by Marny Sumrall around the book's mission-lock governance framework. Confirms the cohort worked through: fiduciary ranking, embedding mission across the org, mission-related failure modes, and specific legal/governance protections. Also serves as existence proof of Eric's community program.
blockquote: Last week I wrapped up an inspirational six weeks of the Incorruptible Early Stage Founders Cohort. Thanks to a webinar hosted by PURPOSE®, I learned about Eric Ries's new book, Incorruptible, which turned out to be one of the best books I read recently (can't recommend it enough!). Most of all, I finally felt like someone had put into writing everything I had been thinking about building mission-driven businesses that do more than maximizing shareholder value. Eric argues that companies drift from their mission because of "financial gravity," the structural pull of investor expectations and short-term incentives that erodes even well intentioned organizations as they succeed. His answer is to build protection in early through mission-locked governance, before success makes the mission a target worth stripping away.
